newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon should privatise public utilities-banker.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon should privatise public utilities-banker.

text.p: Lebanon must gradually privatise its public utilities as a prerequisite for creating "huge" investment opportunities for the private sector, the president of Lebanon's Banks Association said..
"There are no investment opportunities in Lebanon and we should not deceive ourselves or our foreign partners," Francois Bassil told the leftist daily as-Safir in an interview published on Thursday.
"Privatisation can open up huge investment opportunities," he said, adding that creating investment opportunities in the infrastructure sector should be a priority.

He blamed the absence of a clear government investment policy for forcing Lebanon's 82 banks to invest primarily in Lebanese-pound denominated treasury bills at a time when such investment could only bring in secondary or additional revenues to the banking sector.

"The best investment opportunities for the time being are treasury bills and 65 percent of commercial banks' revenue is coming from the interest rates and the subscription into these bills," Bassil added.
Lebanese treasury bills for three-month, six-month, one-year and two-year maturities currently yield 14.36 percent, 16.48 percent, 17.50 percent and 20.76 percent respectively.

Bassil said the government should stop public borrowing and hand over to the private sector the financing of commercially-oriented reconstruction projects. "The government should adopt a courageous policy that cuts on government borrowing," he said

Net total public debt stood at some 14,971 million pounds at the end of September and net domestic debt reached about 12,434 million pounds, according to the latest figures released by the Bank of Lebanon.
Bassil said the privatisation of public utilities "creates new employment opportunities and lowers the cost of living".

Unemployment in Lebanon stands at 15 percent and the labour force is 45 percent of a population of 3.1 million, according to estimates published in an economic bulletin prepared by a leading Beirut bank earlier this week.
